questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Finding a destination that fits into my needs, combining both academic interests and my personal interests into one. Within Iceland I both had great classes and developed a lot within academia, but I also got to explore the country and enjoy its nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was the student housing, which wasn't very well organised. The classes at the university were easy to figure out, and we got a lot of guidance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Our professors offered a lot of assistance, as well as the student office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I still found my off campus housing through the university. Unfortunately, it is a little disorganised.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most off campus housing in Iceland does not come with any furniture etc., the apartement is completely empty, and it is mostly up to yourself to make the space liveable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were partially registrated online, and had to finish the process at the local student office. This was all very straightforward and well-organised. Mobility Online has so far been the hardest part to navigate of the exchange.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student coordinators were available through email, or you could go to the student office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all my desired classes, as none of them were at the same time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep an eye on your emails, and read them thoroughly as to not miss a deadline.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Some of my classes were tailored to international students, and therefore very easy to follow along with. 
As I took some classes outside my usual studies, I had to get used to some of the requirements within essays etc, but the professors have generally given clear instructions. I have been able to follow along all of them quite well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of my classes had a similar teaching style, with the exception of an online class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Jane Austen and her feminist Legacy
Being Icelandic: Icelandic Folktales, Beliefs and Popular Culture Past and Present
Introduction to the History of Iceland: From Settlement to Modern Times
Conversation I (Spanish)
British and European History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would strongly recommend the class "Introduction to the History of Iceland: From Settlement to Modern Times", as I have learned so much about Iceland and it gave me a good understanding for the country and its culture. The professor I had this semester was very talented, and she teaches a great class.

questions.answer: Furnishing the student apartment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were even more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Through the university gym you could access different classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The swimming pools around the city!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on all the roadtrips you can and see the country, try also to go on some hikes!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, it is quite similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is hard to get in contact with them, I was lucky to find some friends through my classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation of nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the prices and the weather. 
Rent a car with friends and go on as many roadtrips as possible. 
Enjoy the northern lights, so they can make up for the many hours of darkness in the winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finding friends and learning to knit with them, seeing the country and learning new things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The initial loneliness.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
